chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of: from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Sinan, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a junub who sets down the rakwah or the tawr, then inserts his finger into it.
He عليه السلام said: "If his hand was filthy, then pour it out; but if no filth had touched it, then let him perform ghusl from it. This is from that about which Allah the Exalted said:
"He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship."

key_terms.إِصْبَعَهُ: his finger, whose contact with the water is under discussion
key_terms.التَّوْرَ: a basin or larger washing vessel
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.حَرَجٍ: hardship or constriction in religious practice
key_terms.فَلْيَغْتَسِلْ: let him perform ghusl with it

ai.seo_question: Can a junub use water for ghusl after putting his finger into the vessel?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning water used by a junub when he places his finger into a vessel. If the hand bears actual filth, the water is to be discarded; otherwise, the water remains usable for ghusl, in line with the Qur'anic principle that Allah has not placed hardship in the religion.
